full_judgment: 4. Khondker Mahabuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant canvassed that there being no violation of any statute or rule having force of law and there being no concluded contract between the Government and the respondents 1 and 2 creating any right in their favour the High Court Division was in error in granting stay which had the effect of injunction the petitioner per forming a right under concluded contract Mr. Ahmed contended that in view of the proviso of the Specific Relief Act, particularly section 54 and 56, the respondents 1 and 2 were not entitled to any relief by way of interlocutor injunction and as such the order of stay is not sustainable in law, Mr. Ahmed submitted that in the case of Mr. Nurul Islam Vs. Government of Bangladesh (Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 144 of 1976) this Court had expressed the view that the status had the effect of injunction. The learns Counsel submitted that the decision of the learned Munsif was erroneous and the learned District Judge had rightly stayed that operation of order whereas the High Court Division while issuing the Rule had fallen into an error by granting stay of the operation of the order of the District Judge. Mr. Ahmed forcefully argued that the plaintiffs suits are not maintainable either under the Specific Relief Act or under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
